context.full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
context.conclusion: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W of V_K, if W is invariant under x_K,y_K,h_K (the action rho of the Chevalley generators of L_K), then W={0} or W=V_K. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module.

record.type: family of elements of the universal enveloping algebra U(L), indexed by natural numbers
record.definition: X_r=x^r/r! for every integer r>=0, with X_0=1. U(L) is the complex associative enveloping algebra of L. Elements of U(L) act on V through the extension of act. Juxtaposition such as xv denotes this action.

record.type: family of elements of U(L), indexed by natural numbers
record.definition: Y_r=y^r/r! for every integer r>=0, with Y_0=1, acting on V via act.
U_Z is the unital integer subalgebra of U(L) generated by X_r and Y_r for every integer r>=0.
n=lambda+1.
I={i in Z: 0<=i<=lambda}.

record.type: family of vectors of V indexed by natural numbers
record.definition: e_i=y^i v/i!=Y_i v for integers i>=0; only indices in I are used for the candidate basis.

record.type: subring of Q and hence of C
record.definition: R=Z_(p)={a/b in Q: a,b are integers and p does not divide b}. Ring operations are those of Q. All R-actions on submodules of V or C below use this inclusion.
M_R=R tensor_Z M, with scalar multiplication on the R factor.
iota(r tensor m)=r m in V, extended by the balanced tensor universal property. The R-module structure of V is restriction of complex scalars.

record.type: family of complex linear endomorphisms of V indexed by I times I
record.definition: For i,j in I, E_ij is the unique complex linear operator sending e_j to e_i and sending e_k to 0 for every k in I with k!=j. It is defined using the complex basis (e_i) indexed by I.

record.type: family of R-submodules of C indexed by I
record.definition: For i in I, J_i={c in C: c e_i belongs to iota(M_R)}.
J={c in C: c e_0 belongs to iota(M_R)}. When 0 belongs to I this is J_0; the definition does not assume that the different J_i agree.
V_K=V(K)=M tensor_Z K, with K acting on the K factor.
L_K=L(K)=(Zx+Zy+Zh) tensor_Z K, with bracket induced by [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y, [x,y]=h. These integral bracket formulas define the Chevalley construction including in characteristic 2.

record.type: K-linear Lie algebra representation of L_K on V_K
record.definition: rho is the action induced by the lattice operators: for t in {x,y,h}, rho(t tensor 1)(m tensor c)=(tm) tensor c, extended K-linearly to L_K. The action is defined when the lattice operators preserve M and satisfy the Chevalley relations.
x_K=rho(x tensor 1).
y_K=rho(y tensor 1).
h_K=rho(h tensor 1).

record.type: family of K-linear endomorphisms of V_K indexed by natural r
record.definition: X_r^K, also denoted (X_K)_r, is induced by X_r on M tensor_Z K: m tensor c maps to (X_r m) tensor c.

record.type: family of K-linear endomorphisms of V_K indexed by natural r
record.definition: Y_r^K, also denoted (Y_K)_r, is induced by Y_r on M tensor_Z K: m tensor c maps to (Y_r m) tensor c.
F_p=Z/pZ with its field structure for the prime p. For K of characteristic p its canonical embedding in K sends the residue class of an integer to that integer times 1_K.

record.statement: For every semiring A satisfying the strong rank condition, every finite index type T, and every family B_t of additive commutative monoids with A-module structures that are free and finitely generated, finrank_A (product over t in T of B_t)=sum over t in T of finrank_A B_t. Here finrank is the natural-number value of module rank (Cardinal.toNat); the strong rank condition means an injective A-linear map A^a to A^b for finite natural a,b implies a<=b.

record.statement: n=lambda+1>0 and I has n elements. The vectors (e_i)_{i in I} form a complex basis of V. For all natural t, hy^t v=(lambda-2t)y^t v, and for t>=1, xy^t v=t(lambda-t+1)y^(t-1)v. All y^t v with t>=lambda+1 vanish. The generator matrices are xe_0=0; xe_i=(lambda-i+1)e_(i-1) for 1<=i<=lambda; ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for 0<=i<lambda; ye_lambda=0; he_i=(lambda-2i)e_i for i in I. For every natural r and i in I, X_r e_i=binom(lambda-i+r,r)e_(i-r) if r<=i and is zero if r>i; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r<=lambda and is zero otherwise. All these coefficients are integers.

M is stable under X_r,Y_r for every natural r, under x,y,h, and these restricted operators satisfy hx-xh=2x, hy-yh=-2y and xy-yx=h. iota embeds M_R into V; M_R is free over R of rank n and iota(M_R) complex-linearly spans V. Every X_r,Y_r preserves iota(M_R). For i,j in I, binom(lambda,j) is a unit of R; the operators E_ij preserve iota(M_R) and satisfy E_ij=binom(lambda,j)^(-1) X_(lambda-i) Y_lambda X_lambda Y_(lambda-j). In particular Y_lambda X_lambda=E_(lambda,lambda), X_(lambda-i)E_(lambda,lambda)=E_(i,lambda), and E_(lambda,lambda)Y_(lambda-j)=binom(lambda,j)E_(lambda,j).

All J_i for i in I equal J. J is a nonzero finitely generated R-submodule of C. Under iota, M_R identifies with the internal direct sum of J e_i over i in I; Q tensor_R J has rational dimension one and its multiplication map into C is injective. There exists a complex scalar b!=0 such that b belongs to J, J=R b, and (b e_i)_{i in I} is an R-basis of iota(M_R), equivalently its inverse images form an R-basis of M_R.

record.statement: There exists a K-basis beta=(beta_i)_{i in I} of V_K, so dim_K V_K=n=lambda+1>0. It has generator matrices x_K beta_0=0; x_K beta_i=(lambda-i+1)beta_(i-1) for 1<=i<=lambda; y_K beta_i=(i+1)beta_(i+1) for i<lambda; y_K beta_lambda=0; h_K beta_i=(lambda-2i)beta_i. There are K-linear endomorphisms T_ij of V_K for i,j in I with T_ij beta_k=beta_i if k=j and zero otherwise, and T_ij=binom(lambda,j)^(-1) X_(lambda-i)^K Y_lambda^K X_lambda^K Y_(lambda-j)^K. Here integer coefficients are mapped into K, every binom(lambda,j) is nonzero in K, and X_r^K=(r!)^(-1)x_K^r, Y_r^K=(r!)^(-1)y_K^r for 0<=r<=lambda. The natural K-linear isomorphisms V_K -> M_R tensor_R K -> (M_R/pM_R) tensor_(F_p) K intertwine these induced lattice operators; the first sends m tensor c to (1 tensor m) tensor c and its inverse sends (s tensor m) tensor c to m tensor (bar(s)c), where bar:R->K is the extension of the integer map. The second sends u tensor c to (u mod pM_R) tensor c.
